subject: System Design
title: Facebook's News Feed Ranking
description: One-minute skill: Facebook's News Feed Ranking.

hook.text: You have 1,000 friends and follow 200 pages. 1,500 new posts since your last visit. Which 50 do you see first?

buildup.text: Facebook's news feed is not chronological. A ranking algorithm scores every candidate post by predicted engagement.

discovery.text: Signals include who posted it, post type, recency, and your history of interacting with that person's content.

twist.text: Optimizing for engagement creates filter bubbles. Users see more of what they agree with. Controversy gets clicks.

climax.text: News feed ranking balances engagement, diversity, and content quality — a constantly evolving algorithmic challenge.

punchline.text: Rank posts by predicted engagement — not just time.

quiz.question: Why isn't Facebook's news feed chronological?
options: A ranking algorithm shows the most engaging posts first
There are too many posts to show all of them
Chronological order is slower to compute
